title: Code review as a teaching tool

videos.script: Ask a team what code review is for, and they say catching bugs. Count what the comments are actually about, and bugs are about one in seven. {{title}} The rest is the team teaching itself. Naming, questions, other ways to do it. {{counts}} That makes every review comment a small piece of curriculum. This lesson is about writing those comments well. {{example}} A label that says how much a comment matters. A question only when you are really asking. Praise that says what to keep doing. {{labels}} Then the author's half: small changes, a description that answers the obvious question before anybody asks it. And what changes when the author is learning. Fewer comments, chosen, that point at the answer rather than give it.
